findings.evidence: Official scikit-learn documentation states that Brier/log-loss are proper scoring rules but do not isolate calibration alone; calibration curves/reliability diagrams and independent calibration data are needed.
findings.derived: ARGUS should not treat a lower global Brier score alone as proof that PRIME/VALUE probabilities are better calibrated.
findings.hypothesis: Selected-case reliability curves plus Brier decomposition/skill versus baseline will reveal overconfidence hidden by global metrics.
findings.experiment: Shadow-only: compute reliability bins, Brier, log-loss and skill score separately for all predictions and for PRIME/VALUE-selected subsets using time-separated validation.
findings.requiredEvidence: At least 200 settled selected predictions overall before directional conclusions; prefer 500+ and per-market minimums before promotion.
findings.failureCondition: Selected calibration unstable across walk-forward windows or apparent gain disappears versus no-vig/naive baseline.
findings.rollback: Remove selected-case dashboard fields; leave current predictor unchanged.

findings.evidence: SCoRE (2026) develops selective conformal risk control for trusted/positive cases with finite-sample risk control under exchangeability assumptions and extensions toward shift.
findings.derived: ARGUS abstention should be evaluated on risk among accepted predictions, not merely hit rate or volume reduction.
findings.hypothesis: A coverage-risk curve can improve NO BET thresholds without changing the base forecasting model.
findings.experiment: Offline only: rank predictions by existing readiness/confidence signals and plot empirical risk versus retained coverage by market and time window; compare current threshold to conservative alternatives.
findings.requiredEvidence: Multiple walk-forward windows with enough accepted cases per threshold; no threshold promotion from a single season/league slice.
findings.failureCondition: Risk reduction is not stable out-of-time, or retained coverage collapses without meaningful calibration/log-loss gain.
findings.rollback: Keep current NO BET logic; discard candidate threshold.

findings.evidence: A 2024 sports win-probability simulation study shows clustered in-game observations sharing the same eventual outcome can inflate effective sample size and make ordinary bootstrap intervals too narrow.
findings.derived: ARGUS must not count thousands of states from the same match as thousands of independent validation examples.
findings.hypothesis: Match-clustered evaluation and uncertainty intervals will materially reduce false confidence in live/in-play modules.
findings.experiment: Change evaluation only: aggregate/cluster uncertainty by match, report both state-count and independent-match-count, and compare naive versus match-block bootstrap intervals.
findings.requiredEvidence: At least several hundred independent matches spanning score/time/game-state regimes before trusting live calibration slices.
findings.failureCondition: No material difference in intervals and no decision impact; then retain only independent-match count as a lightweight guardrail.
findings.rollback: Revert reporting layer only; no predictor mutation.

findings.evidence: A 2025 axial-transformer football paper reports large-scale recurrent in-game prediction using rich player/team/game state data.
findings.derived: The method is technically interesting but depends on a richer event/player data regime than ARGUS currently proves it possesses reliably.
findings.hypothesis: Adding a transformer now would increase complexity faster than evidence quality.
findings.experiment: None now. Reconsider only after event-state provenance, latency, missingness and replay validation are mature.
findings.requiredEvidence: Stable high-frequency event/player feed, replayable timestamps, independent-match validation and a strong simple baseline.
findings.failureCondition: N/A: rejected for present transferability and stability reasons.

findings.evidence: Official documentation warns that calibrators should ideally be fit on data independent from model training; otherwise probabilities can become biased toward extremes.
findings.derived: ARGUS calibration layers must be temporally separated from model fitting and from threshold tuning.
findings.hypothesis: Strict train -> calibration -> test chronology will reduce optimistic probability estimates and leakage.
findings.experiment: Audit current calibration datasets and attach provenance fields train_end, calibration_start/end, test_start/end; fail closed on overlap.
findings.requiredEvidence: Zero temporal overlap across all evaluated candidate models and reproducible hashes/manifests for each split.
findings.failureCondition: Any overlap or post-event data contaminates calibration; mark affected evidence invalid and rebuild.
findings.rollback: Metadata-only audit is reversible; do not promote any calibrator until clean splits exist.

priorityNext: accepted-risk versus coverage curves for abstention
explicitRejects: Do not add a high-capacity transformer solely because recent literature reports good live forecasting.
Do not interpret lower Brier alone as calibration improvement.
Do not use repeated in-match states as independent sample-size evidence.
Do not change PRIME thresholds from a single short-term ROI slice.
